evidence: The strongest case is: a source seat accepts work, its pane moves, /seat reloads destination state, and a late helper result appears in the preserved transcript. CURRENT-DESIGN.md:19 and DESIGN-NOTES.md:148 explicitly retain that transcript while changing applicable graph state, so the situation is real. But the decisive step—continuing source work as destination work or falsely attributing the helper result—does not follow from either document. DESIGN-NOTES.md:148 expressly disclaims automatic forgetting; CURRENT-DESIGN.md:9 and DESIGN-NOTES.md:149 preserve session/transcript attribution, while DESIGN-NOTES.md:186-188 place project tasks in Beads/native sessions rather than graph. No stated contract says a move cancels an accepted source task or guarantees transparent execution of it by the destination seat. A source-work handoff convention may be useful, but this finding has no end-to-end contradiction of a stated requirement without assuming how an unspecified native session behaves.
